verdict.rationale: WezTerm's own CLI can spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes, and a runtime probe confirmed `wezterm cli spawn --new-window`, `send-text` and `list` working headlessly. A user could script a workspace layout with it, and the Lua config exposes event callbacks via `wezterm.on`. However, the evidence never documents declaring a startup session or layout in config, so the one-command workspace is only implied. Missing for 10: documented config-level startup layout/session definitions (e.g. a startup event that builds splits/tabs), explicit evidence of pane-split scripting, a named workspace concept, and independent corroboration of layout-on-launch workflows.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can define startup sessions and window layouts in config or scripts so a project workspace opens in one command

citations.quote: can be used to spawn programs and manipulate tabs and panes
`wezterm.on` causes your specified `callback` to be called when `event_name` is emitted.
